timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: Platform's checklist will override Trailhead's VAT rule.

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial, one follow-up allowed)
timing.question: Governance by markdown — who audits it?

problem.quote: You get one checklist for both brands, and Trailhead keeps the last word on VAT.

approach.quote: The checklist is a Platform rule, the VAT rule is a Trailhead rule, and CODEOWNERS gives each team its own file.

evidence.quote: for money.ts the resolver loads six files and reports zero unresolved conflicts

next_step.quote: Ask: approve the two CODEOWNERS lines this week.

must_mention.point: Layers add up rather than override so the shared checklist defers on tax and the Trailhead rule owns it
must_mention.evidence_quote: every layer that applies is in context at the same time. So the shared checklist never states tax: it defers to the brand's own rule file, and the Trailhead rule owns tax presentation and rounding.

must_mention.point: A glob rule loads only when a matching path is touched and the misspelt globs meant the VAT rule never loaded
must_mention.evidence_quote: a glob rule loads only when a file it matches is touched, and the misspelt globs meant the VAT rule never loaded at all

must_mention.point: AGENTS.local.md is git-ignored and only changes the sessions of the person whose checkout it sits in
must_mention.evidence_quote: AGENTS.local.md is git-ignored: git status stays silent, and it only changes the sessions of the person whose checkout it sits in.

must_mention.point: A global skill follows one person across projects while the repo skill is shared and reviewed in pull requests
must_mention.evidence_quote: A global skill follows one person across projects; the repo skill is shared and reviewed in pull requests, so I renamed the personal one.

must_mention.point: CODEOWNERS splits the repo layers between Platform and Trailhead while org and enterprise scopes need settings access
must_mention.evidence_quote: CODEOWNERS sends the checklist to Platform and the VAT rule to Trailhead; org and enterprise scopes need settings access

accuracy.anchor: All five points stated with the resolver as proof; the hierarchy explained as additive, not as a winner (anchor: 26–30 = mechanism and evidence both right).

structure.anchor: Outcome → Evidence → Risk → Next action → Ask held in the update; each lead addressed by name (anchor: 22–25 = skeleton intact).

customer_relevance.anchor: The 19% overcharge is implied, not quantified; Jonas's six edit requests never mentioned (anchor: 15–17 = both conditions answered, one number missing).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment within ±5 s; one filler, no tag questions, no long pauses (anchor: 13–15 = on target, fluent).

recovery.anchor: Both objections answered acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer; objection 2 offered CI and enforcement (anchor: 9–10 = calm and evidenced).

stems: "You spent two days unpicking a 19% overcharge; this layout stops…" — open with Dana's number.
"Jonas, your team changes VAT without us because…" — say the six requests out loud.
"The resolver shows zero unresolved conflicts for money.ts, and CI will…" — keep the proof in one sentence.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 03; no previous run to compare with.
